_description: Tiny unanswered observations the player runs into when investigating ambient nouns. Each line is hint-loaded but never resolved — a chair with 'do not move' carved into the underside, a coin wedged behind a brick. The point is curiosity gaps: the world reads archaeologically deep without the engine having to author payoff content. Pure flavor — does NOT set producedSubstantive (so the noun stays repeatable for other verbs and the substantive ladder still gates). Surfaced at ~8% per investigate via narrateAmbientFind.
lines: The {noun} has 'do not move' scratched into the back. The handwriting doesn't match the patina.
A coin is wedged behind the {noun}. Pre-flood mint. You leave it where it is.
Three small notches on the underside of the {noun}, evenly spaced. They count something the marker stopped counting a long time ago.
Someone has tied a faded red string around the {noun}. Reclaimer tag? Forgotten Order vow? The knot is unfamiliar.
The {noun} has been moved recently — its outline in the dust doesn't match where it now stands. A few inches off, no more.
Pressed into a seam of the {noun}: a single fingerprint. Larger than yours. Tartarian Giant, maybe.
There is a smell to the {noun} that doesn't fit the room. Salt and burnt iron. Nowhere else here smells like that.
A hairline groove circles the {noun} at exactly knee height. Something heavy and round was tied to it, once.
The {noun} reflects light wrong. The angle says it should be in shadow; the gleam says otherwise.
Inside the {noun} a small object rattles when you tilt it. The seams are perfect. There is no obvious way in.
Whoever last touched the {noun} did so with gloves. Cleaning gloves — the kind Reclaimers wear to handle relics they haven't tagged yet.
A single hair, not yours, sits across the top of the {noun}. White, long, half-dissolved in mud-glass.
The {noun}'s wood-grain doesn't match the rest of the room. Salvaged from somewhere else. Somewhere south.
Two faint scratches on the {noun} make a shape that could be a child's drawing or could be a sigil. You can't decide.
Beneath the {noun}, in the dust, a circle. Someone stood here for a long time. Their boots left no other mark.
The {noun} is colder than the room. Aetheric, faint. Hold your palm to it and you can feel it pull at your skin.
A single petal — desiccated, blue-black — is tucked into a crack on the {noun}. No flower like it grows in Tartaria now.
The {noun} has been counted. Tally-mark in chalk on its base. Numbers up to fourteen. The chalk is fresh.
Tilt your head against the {noun} and you can hear something. A hum, almost a voice, almost too quiet to be sure.
The {noun} has a small wedge driven into its base. Wood. Old. Whoever wedged it knew the {noun} would otherwise tilt.
A drop of wax, sealed long ago, sits on the {noun}. The impression in it is a sigil you almost recognize.
The {noun} is warm where the rest of the room is cold. You move your hand around it — the warmth is local, palm-sized, no pattern.
Faded chalk on the floor below the {noun} forms an arrow pointing east. Whoever drew it left no other mark.
The {noun} carries a faint Aetheric thrum when you handle it — not enough to hum, just enough to know.
There is mud on the {noun} that didn't come from this room. Different colour, wrong consistency. Carried in.
A pre-flood coin balanced edge-on at the base of the {noun}. Someone set it like that on purpose, and the world has not knocked it over.
The {noun} smells of old paper and metal. There is no paper here. There is no metal here.
Two of the {noun}'s edges have been worn smooth where hands have gripped it many times. The other edges are sharp.
The {noun} is older than the room around it. Forty, fifty years older, by the patina. Whoever brought it here brought a memory in.
Etched faintly on the {noun}'s underside: a date. The numerals are pre-flood; you would not be able to convert them without a Reclaimer's table.
A second hand has corrected something on the {noun}. The first hand's mark is gone except for a faint shadow.
The {noun} has been polished recently. Not by you. Not by anything in this room.
A small dark stain on the {noun}. It is shaped like a hand. The hand was much smaller than yours.
The {noun} has a coin-slot you didn't notice the first time. It is too narrow for any coin you carry.
The seam where the {noun} meets the floor is filled with fine grey-blue dust. Aetheric residue, but old — pre-flood old.
There is a hollow somewhere inside the {noun}. Knock and it answers slightly off-key.
The {noun} has been here longer than the building, but the building was built knowing it would be here.
Pressed lightly into the surface of the {noun}: a fingerprint that hasn't quite faded after a flood and a thousand years.
The {noun} is part of something larger that isn't here anymore. The break is clean, ancient, and not by hand.
Three thin marks across the top of the {noun}, parallel, deliberate. A claim. The faction that scratched them doesn't exist anymore.
The {noun} sits a quarter-turn off from where it ought to. Someone moved it long ago and never moved it back.
A child wrote their name on the underside of the {noun}. The name is in a script you cannot read.
There is something inside the {noun}. You can hear it shift when you tilt it. You don't open it.
The {noun} carries a residue you can taste on the air around it. Sweet. Faintly burnt.
On the floor beside the {noun}: a circle of dry mud where something round has stood. The shape is missing now.
Pressed under the {noun}, half-trapped by its weight: a corner of a letter, sealed, unopened.
The {noun} has been here at least three floods. The strata of mud-glass on its base confirm it.
Whoever set the {noun} where it stands now did so as part of a ritual. The arrangement says so. The ritual is forgotten.
The {noun} responds to your hand a half-second after you touch it. Faint warmth, faint pull. It does it once and then nothing.
There are no fingerprints on the {noun}. Not yours, not anyone's. It has been here, but no one has touched it for a long time.
